recognize_zh: 子宮頸切片下方黏膜被密集淋巴樣細胞浸潤，高倍可見混合的大型活化淋巴球與免疫母細胞；免疫染色（C）呈大片膜狀陽性、EBER 原位雜交（D）見大量散在陽性核，提示 EBV 相關、類似淋巴瘤的反應性病灶。
features: Dense, diffuse lymphoid infiltrate expanding the cervical stroma beneath the surface (low power, panel A)
Polymorphous population of medium-to-large activated lymphoid cells with vesicular nuclei and visible nucleoli, admixed with small lymphocytes, plasma cells and apoptotic bodies (panel B)
Immunohistochemistry (panel C) shows many positive cells with membranous staining in clustered zones (marker not labeled in figure)
EBER in situ hybridization (panel D) highlights numerous scattered nuclear-positive cells of varying size
No sheet-like monomorphic large cell population evident at the magnification shown
describe_en: Biopsy of the uterine cervix shows a dense, diffuse lymphoid infiltrate occupying the stroma. At high power the infiltrate is polymorphous, composed of numerous activated immunoblast-like large cells with vesicular chromatin and nucleoli, admixed with small lymphocytes, plasma cells and apoptotic debris. Immunohistochemistry demonstrates many membranous-positive lymphoid cells in aggregates, and EBER in situ hybridization shows abundant scattered EBV-positive nuclei of varying sizes. In the appropriate clinical context (e.g., primary EBV infection with regression), findings are consistent with an EBV-associated reactive lymphoproliferation mimicking lymphoma; clonality studies and follow-up are needed to exclude an EBV-positive lymphoma.

ddx.vs: DLBCL shows sheets of monomorphic atypical large B cells with destructive growth and clonal IG rearrangement, whereas the reactive lesion is polymorphous with EBER positivity across small and large cells and polyclonality.
NK/T-cell lymphoma shows angiocentric necrotizing growth of atypical cytoplasmic CD3+/CD56+ cytotoxic cells that are nearly all EBER-positive, unlike a mixed B/T polymorphous infiltrate.

ddx.dx: Lymphoma-like lesion of the cervix (non-EBV chronic cervicitis)
ddx.vs: Ordinary florid cervicitis is EBER-negative and usually superficial with well-formed germinal centers.
EBVMCU is a sharply circumscribed ulcer in an immunosuppressed patient with Hodgkin-like CD30+/CD15+ large cells and a peripheral rim of T cells.

captions: A-B: H&E low and high power of dense polymorphous lymphoid infiltrate; C: immunohistochemistry with membranous positivity; D: EBER ISH with numerous positive nuclei
